replace: // the AudioContext constructor is left in place
killedBy: hit-sweep.mjs: removing the AudioContext constructor before boot installs the override on the hit-target context, unconditionally, before it navigates
why: Leaves the two real `AudioContext`s the app builds at boot -- Howler's, when `createAudioEngine` first touches `Howler.volume()`, and `engine.ts`'s `ensureCtx`. On a host whose audio service never connects each constructor returns only after an internal 20-second timeout, so the page blocks for ~40 s before `load` fires and the hit-target driver navigates for ITSELF, separately from `verify.mjs`, so it wedges even when both of that file's page paths are guarded. Issues #781 and #844 are both this file being forgotten while its caller was updated. The find string used to anchor on the `const errors = [];` that followed; the WebGL override now sits between the two, so it anchors on the call alone, which is still the only one in the file.
